title: Getting started with CPLASS
text: CPLASS (Continuous Piecewise-Linear Approximation via Stochastic Search) detects changes velocity within multidimensional particle trajectories. Unlike traditional changepoint methods target changes mean, CPLASS models continuous piecewise-linear anchor trajectory searches space changepoint configurations tailored Metropolis-Hastings sampler. See et al. (2026), Change--velocity detection multidimensional data, full statistical model simulation studies behind method. vignette walks : loading package example trajectory data set; running CPLASS single path; visualizing inferred continuous piecewise-linear anchor path; checking whether search stabilized, running multiple independent starts reliable fit; summarizing fitted trajectory Cumulative Speed Allocation (CSA); running CPLASS small collection paths . CPLASS stochastic search configuration maximizes penalized criterion, Bayesian sampler usual sense. “convergence” always means optimization stabilized (better configuration found), Markov chain reached stationary posterior distribution.

text: main inputs observed time vector t coordinate vectors x, y. Useful tuning parameters: iter_max – total number stochastic-search iterations. burn_in – initial iterations discarded selecting best configuration. s_cap – speed (optional) speed penalty applied. speed_pen – whether use speed penalty (Section 2.3 paper). gamma – exponent strengthened SIC penalty (paper recommends 1.01). pen – penalty choice: "ssic", "aicc", "hybrid". patience – set, stop early criterion hasn’t improved many iterations (see ?CPLASS). fit list tibble inferred segments reconstructed anchor path:

what: 9. Running CPLASS on a collection of paths
title: Getting started with CPLASS
text: batch trajectories, loop paths collect fits. full analysis, prefer CPLASS_multistart() per path single CPLASS() call.
code: path_ids <- sort(unique(traj_data$index_path))[1:3]  fit_list <- vector("list", length(path_ids)) names(fit_list) <- paste0("path_", path_ids)  for (ii in seq_along(path_ids)) {   id <- path_ids[ii]   path_i <- traj_data |> filter(index_path == id)   fit_list[[ii]] <- CPLASS(     path_i$t, path_i$x, path_i$y,     iter_max = 5000, burn_in = 500, show_progress = FALSE   ) } fit_summary <- lapply(seq_along(fit_list), function(ii) {   fit <- fit_list[[ii]]   seg <- fit$segments_inferred   data.frame(     index_path = path_ids[ii],     n_segments = nrow(seg),     total_duration = sum(seg$durations),     mean_speed = mean(seg$speeds),     max_speed = max(seg$speeds),     prop_motile_time = sum(seg$durations[seg$states == 1]) / sum(seg$durations)   ) }) do.call(rbind, fit_summary) ##   index_path n_segments total_duration mean_speed max_speed prop_motile_time ## 1          1         19           29.9 0.19032737 0.4770425       0.62709030 ## 2          2          8           29.9 0.06945923 0.1561290       0.06354515 ## 3          3          6           29.9 0.13308593 0.4942614       0.04682274

title: cplass: Continuous Piecewise-Linear Approximation via Stochastic Search
text: CPLASS (Continuous Piecewise-Linear Approximation via Stochastic Search) R package detecting changes velocity within multidimensional time series, focus intracellular transport trajectories. Unlike traditional changepoint methods target changes mean, CPLASS models continuous piecewise-linear anchor trajectory searches space changepoint configurations tailored Metropolis-Hastings sampler. domain-informed speed penalty discourages biophysically implausible segment speeds, Cumulative Speed Allocation (CSA) statistic summarizes inferred transport behavior without requiring arbitrary motility threshold. Methodological details, simulation studies, applications lysosomal transport, quantum-dot motor assays, EB1-GFP microtubule comet tracking companion paper: , L., , D., Cook, K. J., Shen, Y., & McKinley, S. . (2026). Change--velocity detection multidimensional data.

title: cplass: Continuous Piecewise-Linear Approximation via Stochastic Search
text: penalized criterion can multiple local maxima (see Figure 4 paper), anything going reported result, prefer several independent starts: Summarize fitted trajectory Cumulative Speed Allocation instead arbitrary motile/stationary speed cutoff: See vignette("cplass_example") complete walkthrough, package website published.
code: library(cplass)  # A small built-in example: lysosome trajectories from the cell periphery data_file <- system.file("extdata", "Real_21_Periphery.csv", package = "cplass") traj <- read.csv(data_file) path <- traj[traj$index_path == 3, ]  fit <- CPLASS(path$t, path$x, path$y, iter_max = 5000, burn_in = 500)  fit$segments_inferred          # inferred segments: duration, speed, state plot_path_inferred(fit, motor = "Lysosome", max_speed = 2, path_index = 3) ms <- CPLASS_multistart(path$t, path$x, path$y, n_starts = 5) ms$best$segments_inferred ms$score_spread   # small => starts agree on the same optimum speed_mesh <- seq(0, max(ms$best$segments_inferred$speeds), length.out = 100) csa <- compute_csa(ms$best$segments_inferred, speed_mesh) plot(csa$s, csa$csa, type = "l", xlab = "speed", ylab = "cumulative time")

Default 1/30. iter_max number MCMC iterations. Default 5000. burn_in number initial iterations discarded. Default 500. s_cap maximum segment speed penalty. Default 1. gamma exponent sSIC penalty. Default 1.01 (see Section 3.1.1 companion paper rationale). speed_pen logical; whether activate speed penalty. Default TRUE. Default FALSE. sd optional known noise sd. pen one "ssic", "aicc", "hybrid". show_progress logical; display text progress bar. Default TRUE. patience NULL (default), stop search early criterion score improved many consecutive iterations, rather always running full `iter_max`. title: Run CPLASS from multiple independent random starts and keep the best — CPLASS_multistart
text: t numeric vector observation times. x numeric vector x-coordinates. y numeric vector y-coordinates. lambda_r rate parameter Type-1 (independent) changepoint proposal. Default 1/30. iter_max number MCMC iterations. Default 5000. burn_in number initial iterations discarded. Default 500. s_cap maximum segment speed penalty. Default 1. gamma exponent sSIC penalty. Default 1.01 (see Section 3.1.1 companion paper rationale). speed_pen logical; whether activate speed penalty. Default TRUE. sd optional known noise sd. pen one "ssic", "aicc", "hybrid". n_starts number independent chains run. Default 5. patience early-stopping patience passed chain's MHsearch call. Default "auto": uses ceiling(0.3 * iter_max). Set NULL disable early stopping (every chain runs full `iter_max`), supply number use patience directly. See "Patience + multistart, together". seeds optional integer vector length `n_starts`; `NULL` (default), seeds drawn current RNG state, returned output winning run can reproduced exactly set.seed(result$best_seed). n_cores number cores use via parallel::mclapply() (available Windows; falls back sequential message). Default 1 (sequential). show_progress logical; display text progress bar. Default TRUE.

title: Run CPLASS from multiple independent random starts and keep the best — CPLASS_multistart
text: list : `best`: winning CPLASS output (highest       `best_score`). `best_seed`: seed produced — pass       `set.seed()` re-running `CPLASS()` reproduce exactly. `all_scores`, `all_n_segments`, `seeds`: per-chain results,       inspecting agreement across starts. `score_spread`: `max(all_scores) - min(all_scores)`; small       values indicate starts agree (approximately)       optimum. `patience_used`: actual patience value applied every       chain (resolved `"auto"` applicable), transparency.

title: Run CPLASS from multiple independent random starts and keep the best — CPLASS_multistart
text: default (patience = "auto"), n_starts chains uses MHsearch's patience-based early stopping (ceiling(0.3 * iter_max) iterations without improvement), single chain pays iterations need. Multistart's job make safe: chain independent random trajectory search space, unlikely two different chains plateau exactly (possibly suboptimal) configuration, taking max across chains recovers one early-stopped chain might missed. Empirically (see package's benchmark scripts), `n_starts = 5` auto patience matches best score 5 full-length (-patience) runs almost exactly, fraction time. Set patience = NULL disable early stopping entirely run every chain full `iter_max` (slower, tests find better results default — available want verify data).

text: list `cps_list` (post-burn-trace), `info_table`   (post-burn-diagnostics), `update_info` (acceptance rate),   `stopped_early` / `iterations_used` (whether/patience triggered;   `iterations_used` equals `iter_max` never ).

title: Metropolis-Hastings search over the changepoint space — MHsearch
text: original implementation recomputed full piecewise-linear fit (piecewise_linear_con) three times per iteration: current state, proposal, accept/reject step populate trace. Since fit pure function (t, x, y, changepoints), current state's fit never needs recomputed (identical state fit end previous iteration), post-decision refit always identical either already-computed current proposal fit. version fits proposal per iteration carries accepted fit forward, cutting number `piecewise_linear_con()`/`CS()` calls ~3 1 per iteration. diagnostic trace (`info_table`) also built preallocated vectors instead row--row `bind_rows()`, previously made trace step scale quadratically `iter_max`. Statistically, produces target distribution accept/reject decisions original given stream random draws order. birth-vector proposal now uses stats::rbinom() instead Rlab::rbern(), results bit-identical original code set.seed(), statistically equivalent (Bernoulli draws).

title: Metropolis-Hastings search over the changepoint space — MHsearch
text: patience set, iter_max becomes safety ceiling rather fixed target: running-maximum criterion score (post-burn-) improved patience consecutive iterations, chain stops early. "improvement" idea check_convergence, applied live inside loop pay iterations path need. protect local maxima criterion surface (see CPLASS_multistart ) — chain can plateau local max just easily global one.

Default 1.01 (see Section 3.1.1 companion paper rationale). speed_pen logical; whether activate speed penalty. Default TRUE. sd optional known noise sd. pen one "ssic", "aicc", "hybrid". window_frac fraction post-burn-iterations used "improvement" window. title: Check whether a single CPLASS chain has stopped improving — check_convergence
text: list : `converged`: logical. `best_score`: best criterion score found. `last_improvement_iter`: post-burn-iteration index       running maximum last improved. `iterations_since_improvement`, `window_size`: check's       inputs, transparency. `trace`: tibble `iteration`, `score`, `running_max`,       plotting (see plot_convergence).

title: Check whether a single CPLASS chain has stopped improving — check_convergence
text: runs CPLASS Diagnostic = TRUE, reconstructs trace *accepted* state's criterion score every iteration (`info_table`'s `score_cur`/`score_new`/`decision` columns), checks long since running maximum last improved. nothing better found last window_frac fraction post-burn-iterations, chain flagged (locally) converged. Important: tells *chain* settled, found *global* optimum — criterion surface can multiple competing local maxima (see Figure 4 companion paper), exactly CPLASS_multistart . Use together: size `iter_max` correctly given trajectory length, multistart guard local-maximum disagreement runs.

what: Proposal functions for the CPLASS Metropolis-Hastings sampler — log_q_new_pmf
title: Proposal functions for the CPLASS Metropolis-Hastings sampler — log_q_new_pmf
text: implement four proposal types described Section 2.4 companion paper: (1) independent changepoint draw (`q_new`), (2) birth/death single changepoint (`q_bd`), (3) birth/death segment / paired changepoints (`q_bd2`, via `q_as`/`q_ds`), (4) location shift single changepoint (`q_shift`). `proposal_function()` combines mixture weights `u1, u2, u3`; `pproposal()` evaluates corresponding proposal density Metropolis-Hastings ratio.

title: Proposal functions for the CPLASS Metropolis-Hastings sampler — log_q_new_pmf
code: log_q_new_pmf(lambda_r, dt, N, r)  q_new(lambda_r, dt, N)  log_q_bd_pmf(r, status)  q_bd(r_cur)  q_shift(r_cur)  q_as_pmf(r)  q_as(r_cur)  q_ds_pmf(r)  q_ds(r_cur)  q_bd2(r_cur)  log_q_bd2_pmf(r, status)  proposal_function(u, r_cur, N, lambda_r, dt)  pproposal(u, r, N, lambda_r, r_given, status, dt)

title: Proposal functions for the CPLASS Metropolis-Hastings sampler — log_q_new_pmf

N number observations. status proposal-type-specific status flag returned alongside `r_prop` `q_bd()`/`q_bd2()`. r_cur, r current changepoint indicator vector. u draw Uniform(0,1) selecting proposal type use. r_given changepoint vector whose proposal density evaluated (either proposed current vector, depending direction MH ratio).
